# Work out this month's pay application, retainage included.

> Free pay application generator for subcontractors and small general contractors: paste your schedule of values, set retainage, and get the contract sum, change orders, retainage, previous certificates and current payment due, plus a line-by-line table and CSV. Private, runs in your browser.

Reads the Excel (.xlsx) continuation sheet a contractor already keeps, title block, two-row headers, subtotals and totals row included, in the browser, and checks its arithmetic: a typed-over total, a SUM range that misses a line, retainage that disagrees with the rate.

Handles a retainage reduction at a percent complete either way a contract reads it: the reduced rate on everything billed, or only on work completed after that point, with what was held staying held.

Rolls an application forward to next month: previous takes this period, this period starts at zero, stored stays stored, previous certificates carried exactly.

Downloads the application as an Excel workbook with live formulas (summary sheet linked to a lettered continuation sheet), and offers a free blank pay application template (.xlsx, 30 lines). Own layout; not the AIA G702/G703 form.

PayApps, the hosted pay-app suite (saved jobs, retainage until release, change orders), is open: free on one active job, no card, at https://payapps.marisstella.app/. It imports this tool's Excel workbook as a job's schedule of values or opening balance. Lien waivers, QuickBooks and job costing are in paid plans, not on sale yet.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/)
- [Free pay application template for Excel](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/pay-application-template.html): what each formula in the workbook does and how to fill it in month by month

## Answers

The questions each page answers in its "Common questions" section, with the answer as the page states it. Each link opens that section; the page has the sources.

- [What is a pay application?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/#faq): A pay application (also called a payment application, progress billing or draw request) is the document a contractor sends the owner each period to be paid for the work done so far. It shows the contract sum, change orders, how much is complete and stored, the retainage held back, what was already paid, and what is due now.
- [How is retainage calculated on a pay application?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/#faq): Retainage is a percentage of the work completed and stored to date, commonly 5 to 10 percent. This page multiplies each line's completed work by the work rate and its stored materials by the stored rate, rounds to the cent per line, and adds them. It can also drop the rate once the job passes a completion point, if your contract allows it.
- [How do I fill in the previous certificates line?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/#faq): Take it from your last application: the current payment due that was certified, summed across all earlier applications. If you leave it blank this page estimates it as previous work less retainage at today's rate, and says so in the findings, because that only holds if the rate never changed.
- [How do change orders work?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/#faq): Add each approved change order as its own line with a negative or positive scheduled value, and put CO in the item column (CO-1, CO-2) or in a Type column. They are separated from the original contract sum and shown as the net change.
- [How do I carry the schedule forward to next month?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/#faq): After working out an application, use Next month. Each line's previous column becomes previous plus this period, this period goes to zero, stored materials stay in the stored column until you bill them as installed, and previous certificates become this application's total earned less retainage. Start it on the page straight away, or download the CSV and open it next month. If the owner certified a different amount than you billed, type the certified figure into previous certificates.
- [Can I use the Excel continuation sheet I already have?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/#faq): Yes. Choose the .xlsx file. The page looks through each sheet for the table (a sheet named G703, continuation or schedule first), reads it under the title block and column letters, skips subtotals, stops at the totals row, and tells you if the sheet's own totals or retainage do not add up. An old .xls file needs saving as .xlsx or CSV first. Nothing is uploaded.
- [Is there a free pay application template in Excel?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/#faq): Yes. The page offers a blank .xlsx with an application summary linked to a continuation sheet of 30 lines, retainage on work and stored materials, and every total as a formula. After working out an application you can also download it filled in, with ten spare rows the totals already cover. It is this tool's own layout, not the AIA form.
- [Is this the AIA G702 and G703 form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/#faq): No. It produces the same kind of summary and line-by-line table, in plain text, CSV and Excel, but it is not the AIA form, which is copyrighted, and it is not affiliated with the American Institute of Architects. If your owner requires the AIA form, use the numbers here to fill it in.
- [Is my project data uploaded anywhere?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/#faq): No. The schedule is read in your browser and nothing is sent; a test in the code asserts there are no network calls.
- [What is in the pay application template?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/pay-application-template.html#faq): Two sheets. The Application sheet has the project details and the nine summary lines: original contract sum, net change by change orders, contract sum to date, total completed and stored, retainage, total earned less retainage, previous certificates, current payment due, and balance to finish including retainage. The Continuation sheet has the retainage rates and one row per line of the schedule of values, in lettered columns A to L: item, description, type, scheduled value, from previous applications, this period, materials presently stored, completed and stored to date, percent complete, balance to finish, the line's own retainage rate, and retainage. The blank template has 30 lines.
- [Is this the AIA G702 and G703 form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/pay-application-template.html#faq): No. It is our own layout covering the same kind of summary and continuation sheet. The AIA documents are copyrighted and this template is not affiliated with the American Institute of Architects. If your owner or general contractor requires the AIA form or their own portal, use the numbers from this workbook to fill it in.
- [How is retainage worked out in the spreadsheet?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/pay-application-template.html#faq): Each line's retainage is the work rate times previous plus this period, plus the stored-materials rate times materials presently stored, each rounded to the cent. The two rates are typed once at the top of the Continuation sheet. A line with a different rate takes it in column K, which then applies to both its work and its stored materials.
- [How do I add change orders?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/pay-application-template.html#faq): Add each approved change order as its own row with CO in the Type column (C) and its scheduled value, negative for a deductive change order. The Application sheet sums CO rows into line 2 and everything else into line 1.
- [How do I start next month's application?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/pay-application-template.html#faq): Save a copy of the file. On each line add This period into Previous applications and clear This period. Leave stored materials where they are until they are installed. Type last month's line 6 (total earned less retainage) into line 7, previous certificates, unless the owner certified a different amount. The free pay application generator can do this for you: work out this month there, use Next month, enter the new period's work, and download the result as Excel.
- [Does it work in Excel, Google Sheets or LibreOffice?](https://marisstella.app/pay-application-generator/pay-application-template.html#faq): It should. It is a standard .xlsx file with ordinary formulas (SUM, SUMIF, ROUND, IF). A test opens it in LibreOffice with every cached value stripped, so the formulas have to be worked out from scratch, and checks the summary and each line's retainage against the generator's own arithmetic to the cent. It has not been tested in Excel or Google Sheets by us; both read standard .xlsx formulas.
